questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The possibility of studying composing and arranging as well as sound design and music production was crucial to me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I already was acquainted with Umeå and some people living there so in that sense it was pretty easy for me.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not really receive any assistance - but through the international office I was offered guidance with finding housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I already was acquainted with Umeå and some people living there so in that sense it was pretty easy for me. 
I recommend writing in different facebook groups, for example groups called things as "kollektiv" (communal living), or groups for students looking for housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would say to join student activities so that you can meet other exchange students or local students apart from your classmates - if that is what you want.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Can't really say, since I didn't check them out.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I wanted to study courses that were in Swedish, and those courses were not offered to exchange students. As exchange students you get a link to the courses offered specifically to us, but since I knew Swedish I asked if I could study courses in Swedish. It took some work and a bit of a hustle administratively, but it was possible!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I asked to register for courses in Swedish. Then had to register for a course in english just to be able to start the administrative process, and then later on I could apply for the courses in Swedish. It was a bit of a back and forth but with assistance from the international office and studies administrator I got help, and it worked out.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Assistance via email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100% succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to ask for things that might not seem allowed or possible. Often the administrative system is more 'square' than the actual possibilities and will of the admin staff!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Super competent teachers and fun and challenging assignments throughout the courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were beginner courses at bachelor level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think because of the courses focusing quite a bit on students own styles of creative expression the teachers were a bit more in tune with different styles of expression and music and sound production, and not so strict about learning or following specific musical traditions or rules for composing and arranging music and designing sound. So in that sense the teaching style was different and the relationship between teacher and student felt less hierarchical.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Arranging, Composing and Music Theory 
Music Composing for Film, Computer Games and Theatre

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend both!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really participate in non-academic opportunities at my host university. I found other social activities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really sure.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Go to the communal kitchen in Umeå where a lot of students join for great vegan food. You can also be part of the kitchen team and get to know others! 
Check out all the free museums: Bildmuseet, Kvinnohistoriska, the Sápmi out doors museum. 
The book café Pilgatan is nice, cosy, great books - a lot political and with roots in the north.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Enjoy a forest hike! Go skiing! Read a book at a cosy bookstore, or go to the movies! Get some great vegan food!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Wasn't hard.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to. A lot of students want new friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciate that people in Seden in general appear more open to comprehend as well as defend feminist and norm critical values. I myself have an easier time navigating in Sweden as a queer non-binary trans person.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Ask the administration or your teachers for help whenever you need it or something is unclear! 
- Be open to other ways of teaching and learning.
- Get to know some local students or people -  maybe ask to help out at a concert place, communal kitchen, book store. Make friends!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of. But again my advice is to ask away if you have any concerns or things that are unclear to you about your studies, the structure of your courses, or how to find housing of activities to join.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The teachers, class mates and the fun assignments on our courses.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was composing an adventure theme song for an adventure movie, using all the traditional orchestra instruments.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just a thank you to my teachers and the admin at Umeå University.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
